Daily, monthly, and yearly consumption rates of health decay and cycle count

• Daily Decay = (Initial Health - Latest Health) ÷ Sampling Days
• Monthly Decay = Daily Decay × 30.44 days; Yearly Est = Daily Decay × 365.25 days
• Daily Cycle Consumption = Total Cycle Increase ÷ Sampling Days
• Monthly Cycle = Daily Cycle × 30.44 days; Yearly Est = Daily Cycle × 365.25 days
• Lithium batteries typically decay to ~80% after 300~500 cycles (~4%~8% yearly decay, ~0.5~1.2 cycles/day is normal).
Daily Decay = (Initial SoH - Final SoH) ÷ Sampling Days
Periodic Extrapolation: Monthly = Daily × 30.44 days; Yearly = Daily × 365.25 days
Cycle Consumption: Daily Cycles = Cumulative Cycle Increase ÷ Sampling Days
Periodic Cycles: Monthly = Daily × 30.44 days; Yearly = Daily × 365.25 days
General Reference: Li-ion cells typically retain ~80% SoH after 300-500 cycles (~4%-8% yearly wear is standard).

SoH Core Algorithm & 3 Data Sources Principle
State of Health (SoH) measures the maximum available capacity of the battery compared to its factory rated design capacity.
Based on the BatteryManager framework. Calculates full charge capacity proportionally from current level and charge counter, reflecting factory configs.
Reads Linux kernel driver nodes (charge_full, charge_full_design, cycle_count) and fuel gauge IC registers via ADB privileges for highest precision.
Authoritative getHealthInfo snapshots dumped from system bugreport, containing official Android power management framework health data.

• 95% ~ 100%: Excellent state, almost no battery decay
• 85% ~ 95%: Good state, normal daily degradation
• 80% ~ 85%: Mild decay, slight battery life reduction
• < 80%: Heavy decay, battery replacement recommended
95% ~ 100%: Excellent condition with virtually no battery degradation.
85% ~ 95%: Good condition, representing standard daily wear.
80% ~ 85%: Minor degradation, battery endurance may feel slightly reduced.
< 80%: Significant degradation, battery replacement recommended when practical.
💡 Tip: Full charge capacity fluctuates slightly with ambient temperature (<15°C or >35°C). It is recommended to inspect at room temperature after a full charge.

Charging trends, core parameters, and screen-off efficiency

Power Curve (Amber): Real-time charging rate (W) reflecting fast-charging protocol stages.
Level Curve (Blue): Battery percentage (%) rise curve over time.
Temperature Curve (Red): Cell temperature (℃) and thermal management behavior.
Energy Delivered (Wh): Accurate energy injected into cells computed via numerical integration.
Peak Power (W): Highest instantaneous power achieved during the charging session.
Average Power (W): Full-session mean power reflecting true fast-charging delivery.

• Average Charging Power (W)\n• Time-weighted average power since connecting charger, reflecting energy delivery efficiency and thermal control.
• Peak Instant Power (W)\n• Maximum recorded instant peak during charging session, reflecting fast charge protocol capability.
• Battery Cell Temperature (℃)\n• Real-time sampling by internal NTC thermistor sensor reflecting thermal load. Temperatures above 42℃ trigger safety protection.
• Maximum Temperature (℃)\n• Highest temperature recorded during current charging session to evaluate thermal performance.
• Battery Current (mA)\n• Real-time sampling by coulomb counter / charge sensor. Higher during fast charge, tapering down during constant voltage phase.
• Battery Terminal Voltage (V)\n• Operating range typically 3.4V~4.45V. Rises with charge until cutoff voltage, then enters trickle phase.
• Battery Capacity & Total Energy\n• Charge capacity (mAh) and physical energy reserve based on nominal voltage (Wh = mAh × V ÷ 1000).
• Battery Terminal Power (W)\n• Real-time rate of energy flow at cell terminals (Voltage × Current). Positive (+) indicates charging, negative (-) discharging.
• Charger USB Input Power (W)\n• Real-time physical power delivered from charger to Type-C port. Requires hardware sensor support.

Lightweight · Precise · Modern Battery Analysis Tool

A professional Android utility crafted for precise power consumption analysis, battery health diagnosis, and real-time charging monitoring. Strictly adheres to absolute data authenticity, completely eliminating fabricated, dirty, or mocked readings.

Auto-senses discharge sessions, separates screen-on, screen-off, and deep sleep power metrics with real Wh integration, calculates full-charge endurance from 7-day benchmarks, and provides hardware-accelerated timeline canvas with per-app ranking.
Displays authentic cell and USB port wattage, computes net Wh energy intake via trapezoidal integration, and dynamically tracks power, battery percentage, and temperature in a 3-in-1 chart.
Combines standard Android APIs, Shizuku direct Linux sysfs power supply penetration with fuel gauge IC registers, and stream-parsed Bugreport health dumps for accurate FCC and cycle count diagnosis.
Features persistent foreground service, accessibility auto-healing, PID 1 daemon watcher, and desktop/status bar floating windows for continuous power monitoring.
Fully open source under the MIT License. Sincere gratitude to Shizuku, MPAndroidChart, Google Material Components, and the entire open-source community.

1. Electrochemical temperature and internal resistance models for this device are not calibrated via test benches. The system faithfully displays baseline physical capacity without uncalibrated discounts.

No intentional 0%–100% deep cycling needed. In daily use, having 1–2 natural sessions spanning > 20% will automatically update the profile incrementally.
